long_biography.plain_text:
Café Najjar chairman Georges Michel Najjar invested in developing Raqwa to simplify the preparation of traditional Lebanese coffee. Raqwa uses sealed capsules to preserve the ground coffee’s aroma and prepares a cup at the press of a button. His interest in equipment also produced an earlier patented mechanism that automatically mixed, heated and poured Turkish coffee.

At La Maison du Café, Najjar encouraged customers to explore coffee beyond a familiar daily cup. The tasting salon offered beans from different countries alongside flavoured blends and chilled drinks. Tabletop brewers allowed customers to mix and prepare their own coffee, making individual taste part of the experience.
long_biography.html:
Café Najjar chairman Georges Michel Najjar invested in developing Raqwa to simplify the preparation of traditional Lebanese coffee. Raqwa uses sealed capsules to preserve the ground coffee’s aroma and prepares a cup at the press of a button. His interest in equipment also produced an earlier patented mechanism that automatically mixed, heated and poured Turkish coffee.

At La Maison du Café, Najjar encouraged customers to explore coffee beyond a familiar daily cup. The tasting salon offered beans from different countries alongside flavoured blends and chilled drinks. Tabletop brewers allowed customers to mix and prepare their own coffee, making individual taste part of the experience.
